messages:
alex: hey team — quick q about 429 behavior for per-route quotas + dedicated fallback. If route `payments/charge` is at quota and we transparently route to a lower-capacity dedicated pool, do we return 429 to client, or return 200 with a warning header? this changes SDK retry behavior and user-facing errors.
sam: short answer: try not to return 429 if we can actually serve. 429 should indicate we can't serve at all. But we need client-visible signals so SDKs and observability can differentiate 'served from fallback' vs 'hard reject'.
priya: SDK concern: automatic retry logic is triggered only on 429 + Retry-After. If we return 200-with-warning, clients won't retry and won't surface retry spikes. we want a telemetry signal but not change existing retry semantics.
mike: runtime note: we can attach headers on the response. proposal (single header): `X-RW-Quota: route=payments/charge;remaining=0;source=dedicated-low;est_latency_ms=420`. also add `X-RW-Quota-Served: true|false`? open to simpler.
sam: my preference for contract compatibility:
- If fallback can meet latency SLO -> return 200, include `X-RW-Quota-Source=dedicated-low` and `X-RW-Quota-Remaining=0` so clients/telemetry see it.
- If fallback will violate SLO or capacity is insufficient -> return 429, include `Retry-After` (seconds) and `X-RW-Alternate-Routes` listing non-blocking fallbacks.
priya: that works. additionally, we want a non-retryable telemetry header so SDKs log it but don't change behavior. propose `X-RW-Soft-Quota-Signal: fallback=true` — SDK will ignore for retries but surface in logs/metrics.
mike: implementation detail: keep headers RFC-7230 safe (no multi-line, semicolons ok). concrete example header I will emit when routing to fallback:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-RW-Quota: route=payments/charge;remaining=0;source=dedicated-low;est_latency_ms=420
X-RW-Soft-Quota-Signal: fallback=true
```
and when strict reject:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 12
X-RW-Quota: route=payments/charge;remaining=0;source=global
X-RW-Alternate-Routes: /payments/charge?fastpath=true
```
alex: good. for backward compatibility: priya, can SDK keep current model (only react to 429+Retry-After) and additionally emit telemetry when `X-RW-Soft-Quota-Signal` present?
priya: yes. we'll add parsing for `X-RW-Quota` for metrics but won't change retry logic. we'll also ship an opt-in flag to turn on aggressive client-side retry on fallback in a future release.
devex: docs + changelog: we need a short spec in API docs and a migration note for customers. also add an examples section showing 200-with-fallback vs 429.
sam: I'll open the API contract PR with exact header grammar (BNF of semicolon-delimited kv pairs), two response examples, and a compatibility note. plan to canary for 10% traffic.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: eng-runtime canary -> canary-42 at 2026-04-02T15:30Z :rocket:
alex: follow-ups: - add unit tests in SDK for header parsing - add runtime flag to force 429 for testing - alerting on client retry spike when fallback header rate > 5% of requests
mike: noted. I'll add a runtime metric `rw.fallback.rate` and emit for canary. will also add a lint rule to ensure headers present when fallback path taken.
sam: thanks all — leaving this thread as the async record. I'll link the PR here once opened. :thumbsup:
